evidence: sql_runner.py:129-139 reads SELECT @@SESSION.sql_mode, splits on commas, drops empty entries and entries whose upper-case form is in _remove_sql_modes (stored upper-cased at :78), then runs setup.execute("SET SESSION sql_mode = %s", (",".join(kept),)). pymysql interpolates the one str argument client-side as a quoted literal, so the server receives SET SESSION sql_mode = 'A,B', or '' when nothing is kept. MySQL accepts a comma-separated string literal for sql_mode, and an empty string is valid (it means no modes). The session therefore holds exactly the kept modes. They keep the server's own spelling, because filtering only compares the upper-cased form. The test log asserts at tests/unit/test_safety_rule_sets.py:691 use a fake cursor. The live-MySQL tests in tests/connectors/test_rule_sets_mysql.py:382-407 check the behavior only indirectly, through query results. I did not run MySQL or pymysql. This verdict rests on reading the code and on MySQL and pymysql semantics from knowledge.
